sections.content: Relative clauses let speakers identify or describe a person, place or thing without repeating the noun. Que is the most common relative pronoun, while donde is useful for places. At B1, relative clauses make descriptions more precise and allow information to be connected into longer sentences.

items.spanish: Vivo en una vivienda que está cerca del centro.
items.english: I live in a home that is near the centre.

items.spanish: El barrio donde vivo es bastante tranquilo.
items.english: The neighbourhood where I live is quite quiet.

items.spanish: Mi vecino, que trabaja desde casa, suele estar allí durante el día.
items.english: My neighbour, who works from home, is usually there during the day.

items.spanish: Busco un piso que tenga un entorno agradable.
items.english: I am looking for a flat that has pleasant surroundings.

sections.content: Use que for people and things in many relative clauses, and donde for places. When the relative clause describes something not yet identified, the subjunctive may appear: busco un piso que tenga...
